data.narrative:
Furno Materials is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Gurinder Nagra that has raised $11M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with aligned valuation tiers to support a reliable peer-median approach—zero datapoints survived narrow filtering criteria—making sector-wide median analysis unreliable.

The valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression analysis. This method applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression to the $11M total raised figure as a proxy baseline, yielding an implied valuation of $28M. This reflects the conventional markup from deployed capital to post-seed enterprise value absent market-validated revenue or unit economics.

The triangulated valuation range is $23M to $32M, with a median point of $28M. This narrow band reflects dependence on a single methodology; the range brackets realistic uncertainty around stage-typical multiples rather than convergence across independent validation methods. Key uncertainties include the company's progress toward technology milestones, capital efficiency relative to peers, and the availability of follow-on funding at assumed terms. A peer-median approach becomes feasible only once comparable seed or early Series A transactions in Climate & Energy materialize.
